links.outcome: Objective patient comprehension of brain MRI reports with vs without LLM lay summary
links.effect: Objective comprehension did not differ (58.3% vs 59.4%; OR 0.97; 95% CI 0.90–1.06; P = .54); satisfaction and subjective comprehension improved; normal reports worsened (72.5% vs 76.6%).
links.quote: Objective comprehension did not differ between arms (58.3% vs 59.4%; odds ratio (OR) 0.97; 95% CI: 0.90–1.06; P = .54).

links.outcome: Effect of AI lay summaries on patient comprehension, satisfaction, anxiety in randomized trial
links.effect: No improvement in objective comprehension (OR 0.97); improved satisfaction (64.9% vs 36.7%) and subjective comprehension (50.3% vs 24.0%); anxiety modestly reduced (25.1% vs 26.6%).
links.quote: LLM-generated lay summaries appended to brain MRI reports improved patient satisfaction and subjective comprehension but did not improve objective comprehension, indicating a gap between perceived and actual understanding that should be addressed before clinical integration.

links.outcome: Gap between perceived and actual understanding of AI-generated outputs among patients
links.effect: Subjective comprehension rose (50.3% vs 24.0%; OR 3.17) while objective comprehension did not change (58.3% vs 59.4%); normal reports had reduced comprehension (72.5% vs 76.6%).
links.quote: LLM-generated lay summaries appended to brain MRI reports improved patient satisfaction and subjective comprehension but did not improve objective comprehension, indicating a gap between perceived and actual understanding that should be addressed before clinical integration.
